author: cbsaustin
title: Austin leaders review response, highlight improvements after Sixth Street mass shooting
text:
Austin city leaders are reviewing how first responders handled the deadly Sixth Street mass shooting, highlighting opportunities to improve emergency response s
Police investigate the site of a shooting at Buford's in Austin, Sunday, March 1, 2026. According to Austin police, officers who were already stationed on East Sixth Street arrived at the scene within 57 seconds of the first shots being fired.
While officials noted the quick response, Police Chief Lisa Davis said the department is taking steps to improve deployment times even further in the entertainment district.
“APD has designated a second public safety zone on West Sixth Street to provide faster deployment to the west side of the entertainment district, and this is ongoing now,” Davis said. The Austin Fire Department also conducted an internal review, identifying ways to improve coordination among first responders. Austin-Travis County EMS highlighted how city-supported initiatives helped improve response efforts and the quality of care provided to victims during the incident. The shooting remains under federal investigation.
Chief Davis said she expects the FBI to release its findings within the next few weeks.
